case_title: Randhir @ Randhir Pal & Ors. v. State of Haryana
neutral_facts: The accused were alleged to have been present at a shop on the day of the incident, preventing people from entering the shop and moving on the street. The prosecution's case was based on the statements of two eye-witnesses, who were the brothers of the deceased. These witnesses claimed that the accused were involved in the assault that led to the victim's death. However, the witnesses later admitted that the names of the individuals they claimed were prevented from entering the shop were an addition to their initial statements. The prosecution did not provide evidence to confirm the involvement of the accused in the assault, and the accused were not stated to have caused any injuries to the victim. The trial court convicted the accused based on the eye-witness accounts, but the High Court acquitted one of the accused due to insufficient evidence. The Supreme Court further acquitted the remaining accused, noting that the evidence did not conclusively establish their involvement in the incident.
